title: Weighted emergency quota reconciliation and graceful limiter reintegration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: During cross-region incidents and limiter process restarts we observe prolonged unfairness and SLO churn: some customers lose burst capacity for minutes while others retain excess credits, and reintegrating a restarted limiter causes short overloads and SLO violations. This ticket designs and implements a reconciliation protocol and reintegration strategy to ensure fair redistribution of ephemeral burst credits, bounded transient overload during limiter outages, and predictable SLO behavior during region failover and recovery.
motivation: Reducing customer-visible variance in available burst capacity during limiter outages will materially lower P99 latency regressions and prevent cascading circuit-breaker trips. The goal is to eliminate >5% SLO regression windows caused by limiter restarts and regional failovers and make reintegration deterministic and observable.
proposal_summary: Introduce Weighted Emergency Quota Reconciliation (WEQR): a soft-lease token model with per-customer weight, time-decayed fair-share calculator, escrowed reintegration window, and a two-phase reinsertion protocol. Key pieces: (1) ephemeral soft-lease persisted in distributed store for quick failover; (2) reconciliation worker that computes redistributed credits by weight and recent usage; (3) reintegration handshake that applies a ramped token injection with backpressure-aware canary; (4) circuit breaker integration to avoid overload spikes during reinserts.
design_decisions: 1) Use a small consistent backplane (etcd/consul) to persist soft-lease summaries rather than full per-token logs to keep failover latency <250ms. 2) Compute fair-share using exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of consumption to reflect short-lived bursts while remaining stable. 3) Escrow fraction (configurable, default 20%) reserved for request draining during reintegration. 4) Reinsert tokens in percentage increments with guardrails tied to observed request latency and token-drain rate.
acceptance_criteria: Limiter restart in same region recovers without >3% customer SLO regression compared to baseline in 95% of runs (load tests)
Cross-region failover with WEQR enabled shows <=2x transient increase in error budget consumption vs baseline without catastrophic spikes
No single customer receives >3x their weight in additional burst credit after reconciliation (fairness bound)
Reintegration handshake observable in Console (timeline + events) and logs include tokens_reinserted and reintegration_rate metrics
Automated chaos test introduced to CI that kills limiter process and validates acceptance criteria in simulation mode
tasks: Design proto messages for soft-lease summary (lease_id, region, timestamp, weight, available_credit_summary)
Implement reconciliation worker that reads soft-lease summaries and computes per-customer injection plan using EWMA weights
Add reintegration handshake endpoint to limiter gRPC API (start_reintegrate, confirm_window, cancel)
Modify limiter runtime to support escrowed credits and percentage-based reinserts with backpressure checks
Create observability: metrics (weqr_reinserted_tokens, weqr_backpressure_events), traces, and Console panel
Load test scenarios: limiter restart, multi-region failover, and sustained burst replay; add to pipeline
Write runbook for on-call: steps to toggle WEQR flags, force full-rebuild, and manual reconciliation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reinsert spikes can trigger downstream overload. Mitigation: slow-start reinsertion and circuit-breaker that aborts reinserts when p95 latency exceeds threshold. Risk: state inconsistency between regions. Mitigation: bounded staleness windows and conservative escrow defaults. Risk: increased control-plane load. Mitigation: throttle reconciliation worker and store only compact summaries.
open_questions: What default escrow fraction balances recovery speed vs safety across small vs large customers? (suggest 10-25%)
Should we persist soft-lease summaries in etcd or a dedicated lightweight service with caching?
How to expose per-customer reintegration status to customers without leaking other tenant metrics?
implementation_notes: Prefer Kotlin limiter process changes (existing codebase) and add reconciliation worker as a separate service behind the routing policy. Keep reconciliation interval configurable (default 2s) and add feature flag to enable WEQR per-cluster. Use existing license-keys weights from billing metadata; fallback to default weight when missing.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for EWMA and reinsert planner. 2) Integration tests with two limiter instances using ephemeral etcd in CI. 3) Chaos monkey: kill primary limiter during synthetic burst and assert acceptance criteria. 4) Canary rollout in staging region for 48h with telemetry alert thresholds.
rollout_plan: Rollout in three phases: (A) feature-flagged in staging with no reinserts (dry-run) for 1 week; (B) controlled reinserts in staging region for 48h; (C) progressive rollout to prod by region with canary limiter set (5% traffic) and monitor for 24h before expanding.
comments: 2025-02-20: Initial design draft posted. Feedback from SRE: prefer conservative defaults for escrow fraction.
2025-02-25: Spike completed for reconciliation worker prototype — average compute latency 12ms for 10k summaries.
2025-03-01: First integration run in dev failed due to race in escrow accounting; fixed by making escrow apply to token ledger atomically (PR updated)
2025-03-05: Load test (simulated multi-region failover) shows reinsertion ramping prevented overload; still tuning EWMA decay constant
